With --gaps assume it assumes instead that java.lang.Object.toString() returns a new object, never null: it throws nothing and changes neither its receiver nor its arguments, and the verdict names the assumption

JBMC's counterexample parentBehavior(typed=true) does not reproduce: the method returns true in the interpreter and the property holds on it. The path to it probably goes through what JBMC runs otherwise than the JVM, whatever its class path: stubbed-handler at com.google.common.base.Strings.lenientToString:314: catch (java.lang.Exception) catches java.lang.ArithmeticException, java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException, java.lang.NullPointerException on the JVM, which the program may raise, but JBMC has no class file of java.lang.Exception and its stub has no superclass, so JBMC does not know their classes extend it: the exception escapes the handler; unmasked-shift at java.lang.Integer.formatUnsignedInt:393: shifts an int with >>> by a distance that may be outside 0..31: the JVM shifts by the distance's low five bits, JBMC by the whole distance, so it fills the value with zeros where the JVM does not; unmasked-shift at java.lang.Integer.formatUnsignedIntUTF16:413: shifts an int with >>> by a distance that may be outside 0..31: the JVM shifts by the distance's low five bits, JBMC by the whole distance, so it fills the value with zeros where the JVM does not
